items.detail: Wall Street extended its record run: the **S&P 500 climbed 1.79% to a record 7,737** — its first all-time high in two months — while the **Dow surged more than 900 points (1.71%) to close above 54,000 for the first time ever**.
items.why: Blowout AI-linked earnings from Palantir and Caterpillar combined with fresh hopes for an Iran war deal that dragged crude and Treasury yields lower, reinforcing the risk-on tone.

items.detail: **Palantir rocketed ~29.5%** — its biggest daily gain since February 2024 — after reporting **revenue up 93% to $1.94 billion** and delivering its largest-ever guidance raise, lifting full-year revenue guidance by roughly $498 million to about **$8.15 billion**.
items.why: Surging U.S. commercial demand (up 149%) and the record guidance raise validated the AI-software growth story and reignited enthusiasm for the AI trade.

items.detail: Industrial bellwether **Caterpillar jumped 5.6%** to a record after raising its annual revenue-growth forecast, adding heft to the broadening rally beyond megacap tech.
items.why: The AI data-center buildout has fueled demand for Caterpillar's power-generation and construction equipment, extending the AI-capex theme into the industrial economy.

items.detail: The AI euphoria cracked after the bell: **AMD sank nearly 9% in after-hours trade** despite record **$11.54 billion revenue** and data-center sales that **more than doubled (+107%) to $6.7 billion**, both topping estimates.
items.why: An underwhelming sales outlook and rising-capex concerns disappointed shareholders who had priced in more upside from the AI data-center expansion, a warning sign for Wednesday's session.

items.detail: Oil extended its slide with crude slipping further **below $80**, keeping downward pressure on Treasury yields and the inflation outlook as the rally broadened. Attention now turns to **Friday's July jobs report** as the next macro test.
items.why: Persistent hopes for a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz continued to unwind July's war-driven supply premium, easing the rates-and-inflation overhang for equities.

items.detail: Indian equities pushed higher again on Wednesday: the **Sensex jumped over 600 points** and the **Nifty 50 opened above 24,650** (opening near 24,669), building on the multi-session recovery.
items.why: Crude oil sliding below $80 a barrel kept easing India's import-bill and inflation worries, sustaining the risk appetite that has powered the recent rally.

items.detail: Leadership rotated toward rate-sensitive and cyclical names, with **IndiGo up ~2%** and **L&T up ~1.8%** leading gainers alongside Bajaj Finance, M&M, Wipro and Tata Motors.
items.why: Cheaper crude directly lifts fuel-heavy airlines and rate-sensitive financials and autos, channeling the oil-relief trade into the most exposed sectors.

items.detail: Flows flipped from the prior session's pattern: **FIIs stepped up buying to ₹2,446 crore** on Aug 4 while **DIIs turned net sellers of ₹936 crore** — a marked pickup in foreign appetite as domestic funds booked profits.
items.why: The sustained crude pullback and firmer global risk sentiment drew foreign investors back more aggressively, reversing the DII-led support that had underpinned earlier gains.

items.detail: Crypto finally edged into the risk-on move: **Bitcoin held above $64,000** (near $64,037–$64,266, up ~1% on the day) and **Ether firmed to about $1,864**, both recovering from the prior session's drift lower.
items.why: A steady return of spot-ETF demand and lingering CLARITY Act optimism offset a still-hawkish Fed, helping crypto shake off the earlier de-escalation-driven apathy.

items.detail: The ETF thaw is firming: US spot Bitcoin ETFs logged **~$132 million of inflows across four consecutive sessions**, extending into a **third straight week of net inflows**, though 2026 flows remain net negative at about **$5.2 billion**.
items.why: A modest, persistent return of institutional demand is slowly refilling the year's outflow hole, providing the price support that carried BTC back above $64K.

items.detail: Regulatory hopes cooled sharply: **Polymarket odds for the CLARITY Act passing slid to just 27%** ahead of the Senate's **August 7 recess**, denting expectations for a near-term federal crypto framework.
items.why: With the bill still not brought to the Senate floor before the recess, traders faded the odds of a 2026 passage, removing a potential institutional catalyst.

items.detail: The macro and legislative calendar dominates from here: the **Senate breaks for recess on August 7**, while Friday's US July jobs report and the Fed's **3.5%–3.75%** hold ahead of the **September 16 FOMC** remain the key swing factors for risk assets.
items.why: With no fresh regulatory catalyst imminent, crypto's direction hinges on macro data and rate expectations rather than crypto-specific news.

crossCuttingTheme: Crude sliding below $80 on Iran-deal hopes remained the master switch lifting US and Indian equities and finally coaxing crypto higher, but a new fault line emerged within the AI trade — Palantir's and Caterpillar's blowout guidance drove record S&P 500 and Dow closes even as AMD's ~9% after-hours drop on a soft outlook exposed how much AI-capex optimism is already priced in.
